beats.narration: This is the walkthrough for checkpoint one: fix the broken prompt. If you haven't written your corrected prompt yet, pause here and try it first. Ready? The prompt extracts three fields from a support ticket: category, urgency, and a one-sentence summary. It contains exactly one defect. Did you spot it?

beats.narration: The defect is a missing output constraint. The exact failure mode from the lesson. The original system prompt says: extract the key information. It never says which fields, what values they're allowed to take, or what format the answer comes back in. So Claude returns something plausible, and different, every single run. The fix names everything. Return only a JSON object with exactly three fields. Category: one of billing, technical, escalation. Urgency: one of low, medium, high, critical. Summary: a single sentence. Return only the JSON. No other text. Now every run yields one predictable object: category technical, urgency critical, and a one-line summary.

elements.code:
System: "You are a support ticket processor.
Extract the key information from the ticket."
        ^ which fields? what values? what format?

"...return ONLY a JSON object with exactly:
  category: billing | technical | escalation
  urgency:  low | medium | high | critical
  summary:  a single sentence
 Return only the JSON. No other text."

beats.narration: If you wrote something different, run this check: did you name the fields? Enumerate the allowed values? Forbid extra text? A constraint that leaves any of those open, leaves room to drift. That's the whole craft: close every opening. Next section: extended thinking.
